sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It's hard to overstate just how important record album art was to music before we downloaded everything.
sentences.zh: 在一切都可以下载之前，唱片封套艺术对音乐有多重要，怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: Our experience with a record or CD used to be visual.
sentences.zh: 我们对唱片或CD的体验曾经是视觉上的。

sentences.en: The design of the record cover was your first impression of what was to come.
sentences.zh: 唱片封套的设计是你对即将到来的音乐的第一印象。

sentences.en: I would stare at the fonts on the cover and pour over the liner notes the first time I put an album on.
sentences.zh: 我第一次放唱片时，会盯着封套上的字体，仔细研读内页说明。

sentences.en: It was a ritual.
sentences.zh: 这是一种仪式。

sentences.en: I'm not saying that era of music was better.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说那个时代的音乐更好。

sentences.en: It wasn't.
sentences.zh: 并非如此。

sentences.en: It was just different.
sentences.zh: 只是不同而已。

sentences.en: The art on the records tried to encapsulate the essence of a band and then that essence was transferred to you because you were a fan and it became part of your identity too.
sentences.zh: 唱片上的艺术试图概括乐队的精髓，然后这种精髓会传递给你，因为你是粉丝，它也成了你身份的一部分。

sentences.en: At least that's what it felt like.
sentences.zh: 至少感觉是这样。

sentences.en: Album art was certainly important to my friend and reporter Sean Cole.
sentences.zh: 唱片封套艺术对我的朋友兼记者肖恩·科尔来说无疑很重要。

sentences.en: One certain album and one certain band in particular.
sentences.zh: 尤其是某一张特定的唱片和某一支特定的乐队。

sentences.en: Roman, were you ever a Devo fan?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你曾经是Devo乐队的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: I was more of a Devo appreciator.
sentences.zh: 我更多算是Devo的欣赏者。

sentences.en: I don't think I was really a fan.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我真的是他们的粉丝。

sentences.en: I liked the songs I heard.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我听过的那些歌。

sentences.en: I remember Whippet when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候听过《Whip It》。

sentences.en: You were not a devotee.
sentences.zh: 你不是他们的忠实拥趸。

sentences.en: No, I was not a devotee.
sentences.zh: 不，我不是。

sentences.en: I remember the Red Hats.
sentences.zh: 我记得“红帽子”。

sentences.en: And I have a particular memory of them doing a cover of I Can't Get No Satisfaction by the Rolling Stones on Saturday Night Live wearing these yellow hazmat suits.
sentences.zh: 我还特别记得他们在《周六夜现场》节目里穿着黄色防护服翻唱滚石乐队的《(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction》。

sentences.en: They were really weird.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很怪。

sentences.en: Yes, weird.
sentences.zh: 没错，很怪。

sentences.en: So this story is about that Devo album, the one that they were promoting on that Saturday Night Live performance you saw.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事就是关于那张Devo唱片的，就是你在那场《周六夜现场》表演中看到的他们正在宣传的那张。

sentences.en: More specifically,
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，

sentences.en: it's about the album art of that record because the story of the image that ultimately ended up on the cover of that record is this crazy rabbit hole that I fell down.
sentences.zh: 是关于那张唱片的封套艺术，因为最终出现在封套上的那张图片的来历，是我陷入的一个疯狂的兔子洞。

sentences.en: But before we get there, I just need to cover some things about Devo that you might not know.
sentences.zh: 但在进入正题之前，我需要先讲一些你可能不知道的关于Devo的事情。

sentences.en: Do you know where the name comes from?
sentences.zh: 你知道这个名字的由来吗？

sentences.en: I do not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So a lot of people think of Devo as this really silly, you know, nutty band and jumping around.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为Devo是一支非常傻、非常疯狂、喜欢蹦蹦跳跳的乐队。

sentences.en: But they were actually very serious and had a very considered philosophy.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他们非常严肃，有着非常深思熟虑的哲学思想。

sentences.en: And that was that the human race is in a state of de-evolution, hence Devo.
sentences.zh: 那就是人类正处于“去进化”（de-evolution）的状态，所以叫Devo。

sentences.en: So their songs are all, other than Whippet, like their songs are mostly about corporate control and blind conformity.
sentences.zh: 所以除了《Whip It》，他们的歌大多是关于企业控制和盲目从众的。

sentences.en: And they were actually visual artists before they, before they wrote any songs.
sentences.zh: 而且在他们写歌之前，他们实际上是视觉艺术家。

sentences.en: This was in the early 70s in Akron, Ohio.
sentences.zh: 那是70年代初的俄亥俄州阿克伦。

sentences.en: So I talk with one of the founders of Devo, Jerry Casali, who says like back then they were, they were mostly trying to figure out what de-evolutionary art would look like.
sentences.zh: 我采访了Devo的创始人之一杰里·卡萨利，他说当时他们主要是在试图弄清楚“去进化艺术”会是什么样子。

sentences.en: You know, because we were very, very enamored and put off at the same time by pop culture, like the lowest end of like ad graphics, terrible TV commercials.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为我们一方面非常迷恋流行文化，另一方面又对它感到厌恶，比如最底层的广告图形、糟糕的电视广告。

sentences.en: We were kind of drawn to kitsch.
sentences.zh: 我们有点被媚俗的东西吸引了。

sentences.en: And occasionally they would go out shopping for kitsch.
sentences.zh: 偶尔他们会出去采购这些媚俗的东西。

sentences.en: So we're walking through the Kmart.
sentences.zh: 我们当时正走在凯马特（Kmart）里。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: It was the predecessor to Kmart.
sentences.zh: 那是凯马特的前身。

sentences.en: It was Click.
sentences.zh: 叫Click。

sentences.en: And this is Mark Mothersbaugh.
sentences.zh: 这位是马克·马瑟斯鲍。

sentences.en: He's another member of the band.
sentences.zh: 他是乐队的另一名成员。

sentences.en: This is probably the point to mention that this was more than four decades ago and not everybody's memory is too clear.
sentences.zh: 现在大概应该提一下，这已经是四十多年前的事了，不是每个人的记忆都那么清晰。

sentences.en: So independent of what department store they're in, they're in a department store.
sentences.zh: 所以不管他们在哪个百货商店，反正他们是在一家百货商店里。

sentences.en: They are in a department store.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是在一家百货商店里。

sentences.en: We were looking for supplies.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在找补给品。

sentences.en: We were collaborating on a visual art piece together and walking through the sports section.
sentences.zh: 我们正在合作一件视觉艺术作品，走在体育用品区。

sentences.en: And there's these six practice golf balls in a clear plastic pouch, sealed shut at the top with a cardboard display head.
sentences.zh: 那里有六个练习高尔夫球，装在一个透明塑料袋里，顶部用纸板展示头密封着。

sentences.en: Phil, can you picture this?
sentences.zh: 菲尔，你能想象这个画面吗？

sentences.en: It's like that display head with the hole in it that hangs on a hook.
sentences.zh: 就像那种带孔的展示头，可以挂在钩子上。

sentences.en: Yes, I can picture it.
sentences.zh: 是的，我能想象出来。

sentences.en: Kind of like the racks with bags of generic candy at the gas station, like a clear bag full of candy.
sentences.zh: 有点像加油站里挂着的一袋袋散装糖果，那种装满糖果的透明袋子。

sentences.en: And it just says gummy bears at the top.
sentences.zh: 顶部就写着“软糖熊”。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So on that display head is an illustration of the smiling face of Chi Chi Rodriguez.
sentences.zh: 所以那个展示头上印着奇奇·罗德里格斯的笑脸插图。

sentences.en: And who was Chi Chi Rodriguez?
sentences.zh: 奇奇·罗德里格斯是谁？

sentences.en: Chi Chi Rodriguez is one of the most famous golfers in history.
sentences.zh: 奇奇·罗德里格斯是历史上最著名的高尔夫球手之一。

sentences.en: He was like, I don't know what Chi Chi Rodriguez was like.
sentences.zh: 他就像是……我不知道奇奇·罗德里格斯是什么样的。

sentences.en: He was like the Elvis of golfers.
sentences.zh: 他就像高尔夫球手里的猫王。

sentences.en: He was just like a big showman.
sentences.zh: 他就是一个大表演家。

sentences.en: I saw it and I just loved it.
sentences.zh: 我看到了，我就爱上了它。

sentences.en: It was a picture of him in front of a golf ball.
sentences.zh: 那是一张他在高尔夫球前的照片。

sentences.en: So his head's kind of haloed by a big golf ball.
sentences.zh: 他的头被一个大高尔夫球衬托着，像是有个光环。

sentences.en: Kind of imitating something that I'd already been printing, which was human heads in front of the moon.
sentences.zh: 有点模仿我当时已经在印刷的东西，也就是人头在月亮前面的图案。

sentences.en: And it made us laugh.
sentences.zh: 这让我们笑了。

sentences.en: We chuckle.
sentences.zh: 我们咯咯笑。

sentences.en: We have to have that.
sentences.zh: 我们必须拥有它。

sentences.en: And of course, golf was almost symbolically like the most lame kind of, you know, bourgeois pursuit that you could have, especially at that time.
sentences.zh: 当然，高尔夫在象征意义上几乎是当时你能想到的最无聊、最资产阶级的追求。

sentences.en: Unless your parents were rich, you didn't get to go golfing.
sentences.zh: 除非你父母很有钱，否则你没机会去打高尔夫。

sentences.en: If we ever imagined ourself on a golf course, it was probably as a caddy.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想象自己出现在高尔夫球场上，那大概也是作为球童。

sentences.en: And how boring it looked then on TV and the announcing.
sentences.zh: 而且当时在电视上看到它和解说时，显得多么无聊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the one guy who stood out was Chi Chi because he didn't fit with the rest of the golfers at all.
sentences.zh: 但奇奇是唯一一个脱颖而出的人，因为他一点也不像其他高尔夫球手。

sentences.en: He wore these loud pants and bright shirts.
sentences.zh: 他穿着花哨的裤子和鲜艳的衬衫。

sentences.en: And he had this famous hat that only he wore, which had a specific hat band and, you know, a straw Panama kind of hat.
sentences.zh: 他戴着那顶只有他才戴的著名帽子，那是一种有特定帽带的巴拿马草帽。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So did they buy those golf balls?
sentences.zh: 所以他们买了那些高尔夫球吗？

sentences.en: They bought the golf balls.
sentences.zh: 他们买了那些高尔夫球。

sentences.en: Mark used the Chi Chi image in a manifesto he was writing about being a, quote unquote, spud boy in the rubber town of Akron.
sentences.zh: 马克在他写的一篇关于在阿克伦橡胶城做一个“土豆男孩”的宣言中使用了奇奇的形象。

sentences.en: But other than that, nothing really happened with it until we were already putting out our self-produced single, Be Stiff.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，直到我们发行自制的单曲《Be Stiff》之前，并没有发生什么特别的事。

sentences.en: Oh, I like that song.
sentences.zh: 哦，我喜欢那首歌。

sentences.en: It's it.
sentences.zh: 就是它。

sentences.en: This is my favorite one.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的一首。

sentences.en: So it's it's like this kind of jokey anthem celebrating like literal stiffness, like uptightness, talking about televangelists, politicians and how stiff they are.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一首讽刺赞歌，歌颂那种字面意义上的“僵硬”，也就是死板，谈论电视布道者、政客以及他们有多么僵硬。

sentences.en: And somehow, and I don't really remember the moment, but we had the idea of putting Chi Chi on that cover.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，我不记得具体时刻了，但我们想到了把奇奇放在封套上。

sentences.en: And so they used that picture of Chi Chi on the cover of the 45 of the single.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把那张奇奇的照片用在了那张45转单曲唱片的封套上。

sentences.en: And it was like this commentary on on on commercialism and, you know, our obsession with selling.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对商业主义以及我们对销售的痴迷的一种评论。

sentences.en: And in this case, selling plastic golf balls and the Americana of the golfer.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，就是销售塑料高尔夫球和高尔夫球手的美国文化。

sentences.en: So Be Stiff comes out in 1978.
sentences.zh: 所以《Be Stiff》在1978年发行了。

sentences.en: And, you know, they're still not famous.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们当时还不红。

sentences.en: Yes, they're this obscure art rock band.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们是一支默默无闻的艺术摇滚乐队。

sentences.en: But then about four months later, Devo gets their big break.
sentences.zh: 但大约四个月后，Devo迎来了他们的重大突破。

sentences.en: Warner Brothers signed the band to their first full length album.
sentences.zh: 华纳兄弟签下了他们，为他们制作第一张全长专辑。

sentences.en: And that, according to Jerry, is where the real de-evolution began.
sentences.zh: 而据杰里说，真正的“去进化”就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: We've laid that whole thing out and working up to this moment.
sentences.zh: 我们已经铺垫了这一切，并为这一刻做好了准备。

sentences.en: And then comes the real Devo twist that only a corporation could provide.
sentences.zh: 然后就出现了只有大公司才能带来的真正的Devo式转折。

sentences.en: In other words, what we're talking about, we become part of.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们所谈论的东西，我们自己也成了其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So they're about to be on top 40 radio and broadcast on the TV screens of middle America.
sentences.zh: 所以他们即将登上四十强电台，并在美国中产阶级的电视屏幕上播出。

sentences.en: What was that first record called?
sentences.zh: 那张唱片叫什么名字？

sentences.en: It's a long title.
sentences.zh: 标题很长。

sentences.en: It's called Question, Are We Not Men?
sentences.zh: 叫《Question, Are We Not Men?》

sentences.en: Answer, We Are Devo.
sentences.zh: 回答，我们是 Devo。

sentences.en: And this is their first major label album.
sentences.zh: 这是他们在大厂牌发行的第一张专辑。

sentences.en: This is their firSt.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的第一张。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So Mark and Jerry and the other members of the band, they're like, well, that picture of Chi-Chi worked so well on the single.
sentences.zh: 所以马克、杰里和乐队的其他成员觉得，奇奇的那张照片在单曲封套上效果很好。

sentences.en: Let's just stick with it.
sentences.zh: 我们就继续用它吧。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of our brand now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这现在算是我们的品牌了。

sentences.en: Let's just put that on the cover of the full length record.
sentences.zh: 我们就把它放在全长专辑的封套上吧。

sentences.en: And this is like a picture of Chi-Chi Rodriguez.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一张奇奇·罗德里格斯的照片。

sentences.en: The original picture from that thing they bought at Kmart.
sentences.zh: 就是他们从凯马特买回来的那个东西上的原始照片。

sentences.en: They just took that, lifted it directly and put it onto their album.
sentences.zh: 他们直接拿过来，原封不动地放到了他们的专辑上。

sentences.en: And they're going to put that now on a major label album.
sentences.zh: 现在他们要把它放到一张大厂牌专辑上了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So they head to California, you know, movie montage theme music here, Beverly Hillbillies, whatever.
sentences.zh: 于是他们前往加州，（此处应有电影蒙太奇主题音乐，比如《贝弗利山人》之类的）。

sentences.en: And they go to Warner Brothers HQ.
sentences.zh: 他们去了华纳兄弟总部。

sentences.en: And this is like the process back then.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时的流程。

sentences.en: And maybe now, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 也许现在也是，我不知道。

sentences.en: But like they're heading from department to department and Warner Brothers, you know, dealing with all of the new album things that need to happen.
sentences.zh: 他们从一个部门走到另一个部门，处理所有需要完成的新专辑事务。

sentences.en: And we're told to go see, I think Rick Serrini was his name and he seemed to be an okay guy.
sentences.zh: 我们被告知去见一位叫里克·塞里尼的人，他看起来是个不错的人。

sentences.en: He's in the art department.
sentences.zh: 他在艺术部门。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's the head of the art department.
sentences.zh: 他是艺术部门的负责人。

sentences.en: I was creative director at Warner Brothers Records.
sentences.zh: 我当时是华纳兄弟唱片的创意总监。

sentences.en: He seemed to like what we were up to.
sentences.zh: 他似乎很喜欢我们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: The one band that I appreciated the most was Devo.
sentences.zh: 我最欣赏的一支乐队就是Devo。

sentences.en: I love the fact that they just never took anything very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他们从不把任何事情看得太严肃这一点。

sentences.en: Do you remember that first meeting with them?
sentences.zh: 你还记得第一次见他们吗？

sentences.en: Not only do I remember it, I have a Polaroid of it.
sentences.zh: 我不但记得，我还有一张当时的拍立得照片。

sentences.en: We show him the image, he chuckles.
sentences.zh: 我们给他看了那张图，他咯咯笑了。

sentences.en: I thought it was clip art.
sentences.zh: 我以为那是剪贴画。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Chi-Chi does look a lot like clip art.
sentences.zh: 奇奇看起来确实很像剪贴画。

sentences.en: And I guess I never asked.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时没问。

sentences.en: I only found out that it was him sometime later.
sentences.zh: 我是后来才知道那是他的。

sentences.en: Well, I guess what did it evoke for you?
sentences.zh: 那么，它让你联想到了什么？

sentences.en: Absurdity.
sentences.zh: 荒诞感。

sentences.en: I mean, you have to think about what was going on back in the day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你得想想当时的情况。

sentences.en: Artwork, you know, on album covers had rules attached to it.
sentences.zh: 唱片封套上的艺术作品是有规则限制的。

sentences.en: Most of the albums were delivered to little mom and pop music stores all around the country.
sentences.zh: 大多数唱片会被送到全国各地的小型夫妻音乐店。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there'd be some kid who would come in at four o'clock after school.
sentences.zh: 会有个孩子在放学后四点钟进来。

sentences.en: And his job was to open up the box of records from Warner Brothers or Columbia or whatnot and then rack them.
sentences.zh: 他的工作就是打开华纳兄弟或哥伦比亚唱片公司寄来的唱片箱，然后把它们上架。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the one thing that they told all of us in the art department is don't screw that up.
sentences.zh: 艺术部门告诉我们所有人的一件事就是：千万别搞砸了。

sentences.en: A rock band has to look like a rock band.
sentences.zh: 摇滚乐队就得有摇滚乐队的样子。

sentences.en: A country western has to look like country western.
sentences.zh: 乡村音乐乐队就得有乡村音乐乐队的样子。

sentences.en: They better have cowboy hats on.
sentences.zh: 他们最好戴上牛仔帽。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they get misracked.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们会被放错货架。

sentences.en: What we were put through by David Berman actually achieved something here better than just using a found image.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伯曼（David Berman）让我们经历的这一切，实际上比单纯使用一张现成的照片取得了更好的效果。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is corporate interference, plus the faces of four American presidents who prosecuted the Vietnam War and its aftermath,
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，企业干预，加上四位曾发动越南战争及其后续影响的美国总统的脸，

sentences.en: and this wonderfully dandy-ish golf legend, all of those together.
sentences.zh: 还有这位风度翩翩的高尔夫传奇人物，所有这些加在一起。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's more Devo than the original Chi-Chi image, in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这比最初的奇奇照片更具 Devo 的风格。

sentences.en: That's what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我就是这个意思。

sentences.en: It's Devo in action.
sentences.zh: 这就是行动中的 Devo。

sentences.en: Like, do you need an example of what we're talking about?
sentences.zh: 比如，你需要一个我们所谈论内容的例子吗？

sentences.en: Here it is.
sentences.zh: 就在这儿。

sentences.en: So this whole story takes place at the beginning of Devo's career, and they go on to play for decades, extremely famous.
sentences.zh: 所以整个故事发生在 Devo 职业生涯的初期，他们后来表演了几十年，非常出名。

sentences.en: They were just nominated to be in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚被提名进入摇滚名人堂。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do they think about Chi-Chi as part of their origin story?
sentences.zh: 他们认为奇奇是他们起源故事的一部分吗？

sentences.en: You know, Mark Mothersbaugh actually sort of raised that when we were talking.
sentences.zh: 你知道，马克·马瑟斯鲍夫（Mark Mothersbaugh）在我们交谈时确实提到了这一点。

sentences.en: I really, I don't think anybody ever tried to measure how much that album cover had in the success of Devo, but it could possibly have been the tipping stone that just, like,
sentences.zh: 我真的，我不认为有人曾试图衡量那张专辑封面在 Devo 的成功中占了多大比重，但它很可能是那个转折点，就像，

sentences.en: changed everything and gave us a chance to have a public career.
sentences.zh: 改变了一切，让我们有机会拥有公开的职业生涯。

sentences.en: So, just in case, thank you, Chi-Chi.
sentences.zh: 所以，以防万一，谢谢你，奇奇。

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼（Roman）。

sentences.en: Yeah?
sentences.zh: 怎么了？

sentences.en: Story's not over.
sentences.zh: 故事还没结束。

sentences.en: There's one more diabolical Devo twiSt.
sentences.zh: 还有一个更魔鬼的 Devo 转折。

sentences.en: Here's Derek Asali.
sentences.zh: 这是德里克·阿萨利（Derek Asali）。

sentences.en: I have to say that now that I'm a senior citizen, I completely changed my attitude about the game of golf.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，现在我成了老年人，我对高尔夫这项运动的态度完全改变了。

sentences.en: You did not, really?
sentences.zh: 你没有吧，真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I like it now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我现在喜欢它了。

sentences.en: I really, it's changed so much from those days and who got to play it and how it's played.
sentences.zh: 真的，它和当年相比变化太大了，包括谁能玩它以及它是怎么玩的。

sentences.en: I mean, those guys really are athletes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那些家伙确实是运动员。

sentences.en: I never thought I would hear a member of Devo say that.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过会听到 Devo 的成员这么说。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Here's a doubly hideous secret unfolding right now.
sentences.zh: 现在正揭开一个双重丑陋的秘密。

sentences.en: I really like professional football.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢职业橄榄球。

sentences.en: A version of this piece originally aired on the NPR sports show Only a Game.
sentences.zh: 本节目的一个版本最初在 NPR 体育节目《Only a Game》中播出。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Gary Wallach, who conceived of the story, and Hugh Brown, who helped Sean Cole with the research.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢构思了这个故事的加里·沃拉赫（Gary Wallach），以及协助肖恩·科尔（Sean Cole）进行研究的休·布朗（Hugh Brown）。

sentences.en: Around the time Devo was putting out their first singles in the mid-1970s, a music teacher in Canada was making his own DIY records with a bunch of his elementary school students,
sentences.zh: 大约在 20 世纪 70 年代中期 Devo 发行首批单曲时，加拿大的一位音乐老师正带着他的一群小学生制作自己的 DIY 唱片，

sentences.en: and the result was a haunting and uplifting outsider art masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 结果是一部令人难忘且振奋人心的局外人艺术杰作。

sentences.en: That story, after this.
sentences.zh: 那个故事，稍后播出。

sentences.en: In Canada, in the 1970s, a music teacher named Hans Finger recorded 60 of his elementary school students singing in a gymnasium.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 70 年代的加拿大，一位名叫汉斯·芬格（Hans Finger）的音乐老师录制了 60 名小学生在体育馆里唱歌的录音。

sentences.en: He pressed a few vinyl records of those recordings and handed them out to parents.
sentences.zh: 他压制了几张这些录音的黑胶唱片，并分发给了家长们。

sentences.en: The Langley School Music Project was little known until a record collector named Brian Lind found one of those albums in a thrift store in the year 2000.
sentences.zh: “兰利学校音乐项目”（Langley School Music Project）在 2000 年一位名叫布莱恩·林德（Brian Lind）的唱片收藏家在旧货店发现其中一张专辑之前，几乎无人知晓。

sentences.en: Lind shared it with some people and eventually, Bar None Records gave it a proper release.
sentences.zh: 林德与一些人分享了它，最终，Bar None Records 公司正式发行了它。

sentences.en: The record's cover featured a collage of black and white pictures of the students singing, strumming guitars, playing drums, and clapping along.
sentences.zh: 唱片封面是一张黑白照片拼贴画，展示了学生们唱歌、弹吉他、打鼓和拍手的情景。

sentences.en: The album was called Innocence and Despair.
sentences.zh: 这张专辑名为《纯真与绝望》（Innocence and Despair）。

sentences.en: The rediscovered recordings were a hit.
sentences.zh: 这些被重新发现的录音大受欢迎。

sentences.en: Salon music critic Stephen Hyden wrote,
sentences.zh: Salon 音乐评论家斯蒂芬·海登（Stephen Hyden）写道：

sentences.en: The gloomy title Innocence and Despair is no lie.
sentences.zh: 阴郁的标题《纯真与绝望》所言非虚。

sentences.en: The echoing, yelping renditions of this feel-good music gives off a powerfully aching melancholy.
sentences.zh: 这些令人愉悦的音乐中回荡着尖叫般的演绎，散发出一种强烈而痛苦的忧郁。

sentences.en: It's the sound of youth, frozen on tape, as it fades inexorably away.
sentences.zh: 这是青春的声音，被冻结在磁带上，随着它不可阻挡地消逝。

sentences.en: Here's the music teacher from the Langley School Music Project, Hans Finger, talking to Katie Mingle in 2010.
sentences.zh: 这是“兰利学校音乐项目”的音乐老师汉斯·芬格，2010 年与凯蒂·明格尔（Katie Mingle）的谈话。

sentences.en: Before I was teaching in Langley, I played in a heavy metal band.
sentences.zh: 在兰利教书之前，我在一支重金属乐队里演奏。

sentences.en: It never occurred to me to be a teacher.
sentences.zh: 我从未想过要当老师。

sentences.en: I wasn't really a good student myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己其实也不是个好学生。

sentences.en: And the kids were okay, but I wasn't all that gushy about them, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 孩子们还行，但老实说，我并没有对他们表现出太多的热情。

sentences.en: I knew nothing about kids' music.
sentences.zh: 我对儿童音乐一无所知。

sentences.en: I knew nothing about teaching.
sentences.zh: 我对教学一无所知。

sentences.en: I knew nothing about anything.
sentences.zh: 我对任何事情都一无所知。

sentences.en: You know, I had hair.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那时我有头发。

sentences.en: I had attitude.
sentences.zh: 我有态度。

sentences.en: I weighed 98 pounds.
sentences.zh: 我体重 98 磅。

sentences.en: But off I went to Langley, and I started teaching.
sentences.zh: 但我还是去了兰利，开始教书。

sentences.en: I was hippy-dippy.
sentences.zh: 我当时是个嬉皮士。

sentences.en: I had really no philosophy at all about teaching.
sentences.zh: 我真的没有任何教学理念。

sentences.en: I had, I can't really say I thought about it a lot, you know.
sentences.zh: 我，我真的不能说我考虑过很多，你知道。

sentences.en: I had a lot of ideas about music, but certainly not about teaching.
sentences.zh: 我对音乐有很多想法，但对教学绝对没有。

sentences.en: You know, for me, I mean, I've been playing in bands since I was like 11 or 12 years old,
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，我是说，我从 11 或 12 岁起就在乐队里演奏，

sentences.en: and it wasn't like anyone who taught us.
sentences.zh: 并没有人教过我们。

sentences.en: It wasn't even like anybody said, oh, this is the way you do it, or that's the way you do it.
sentences.zh: 甚至没有人说，哦，这是你做的方法，或者那是你做的方法。

sentences.en: We just sort of did it.
sentences.zh: 我们只是顺其自然地做了。

sentences.en: And I'd been doing music like that since I was a little kid.
sentences.zh: 我从小就是那样做音乐的。

sentences.en: So when I went in to teach music, it never occurred to me that I was going to teach anybody how to read notes,
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始教音乐时，我从未想过要教任何人如何识谱，

sentences.en: or that I was going to teach anybody how to pass a teSt.
sentences.zh: 或者教任何人如何通过考试。

sentences.en: The only thing I ever tried to teach children is really, is just to fall in love with making music.
sentences.zh: 我唯一尝试教给孩子们的就是，让他们爱上创作音乐。

sentences.en: That was always my goal.
sentences.zh: 那一直是我的人生目标。

sentences.en: I just taught songs I knew, and I was very into David Bowie in those days.
sentences.zh: 我只是教我熟悉的歌曲，那时我非常迷大卫·鲍伊（David Bowie）。

sentences.en: I was very into Iggy Pop.
sentences.zh: 我非常迷伊基·波普（Iggy Pop）。

sentences.en: I was into old Phil Spector Records, Brian Wilson.
sentences.zh: 我迷恋老菲尔·斯佩克特（Phil Spector）的唱片，还有布莱恩·威尔逊（Brian Wilson）。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until much later that I realized that the songs were thematic.
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，我才意识到这些歌曲是有主题的。

sentences.en: You know, I had gotten a teaching job originally because I was with my girlfriend,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我最初得到这份教职是因为我和我的女朋友在一起，

sentences.en: and she was having a baby, and I needed a day job.
sentences.zh: 她怀孕了，我需要一份日常工作。

sentences.en: And by the time I got this job, we were breaking up.
sentences.zh: 等我得到这份工作时，我们正要分手。

sentences.en: And I think that in the back of my mind, you know, I was feeling like a little bit loSt.
sentences.zh: 我想在我的潜意识里，你知道，我感到有点迷茫。

sentences.en: Contrary to what people think, a lot of kids aren't that happy.
sentences.zh: 与人们的想法相反，很多孩子并不那么快乐。

sentences.en: They all have troubles.
sentences.zh: 他们都有烦恼。

sentences.en: They've got problems at home.
sentences.zh: 他们在家里有各种问题。

sentences.en: They can feel lonely.
sentences.zh: 他们会感到孤独。

sentences.en: They can feel isolated.
sentences.zh: 他们会感到被孤立。

sentences.en: And the music can conjure up that feeling into them.
sentences.zh: 而音乐可以唤起他们内心的那种感觉。

sentences.en: Now, whether or not they completely, literally understand the words,
sentences.zh: 至于他们是否完全、字面意义上理解了歌词，

sentences.en: I'm not sure, sure, that's so important.
sentences.zh: 我不确定，确定那是否那么重要。

sentences.en: I don't think Sheila, when she was singing Desperado,
sentences.zh: 我不认为希拉（Sheila）在唱《亡命之徒》（Desperado）时，

sentences.en: really knew what a lot of those references were about.
sentences.zh: 真的知道那些歌词指代的是什么。

sentences.en: But she certainly captured the feeling of the song.
sentences.zh: 但她确实捕捉到了这首歌的情感。

sentences.en: When I heard other school choirs and things, we sounded so different and so weird, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我听到其他学校合唱团之类的表演时，我们听起来太不同、太怪异了，你知道，

sentences.en: that I thought, oh, well, we can't be any good.
sentences.zh: 以至于我想，哦，好吧，我们肯定好不到哪去。

sentences.en: I mean, listen to all those people.
sentences.zh: 我是说，听听那些人。

sentences.en: They really know how to sing.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很会唱歌。

sentences.en: So I never thought of it in terms of it was special because it was good.
sentences.zh: 所以我从没想过它之所以特别是因为它好。

sentences.en: I always thought of it in terms of it was special because it was different.
sentences.zh: 我总是认为它特别是因为它与众不同。

sentences.en: Oftentimes, I would have 60, 90 kids in my class,
sentences.zh: 通常，我的班上有 60 到 90 个孩子，

sentences.en: and they'd be all over the place because there was no room,
sentences.zh: 他们到处都是，因为没有空间，

sentences.en: and we'd have instruments, and we had no equipment,
sentences.zh: 我们有乐器，但没有设备，

sentences.en: so I brought in all the equipment from my band,
sentences.zh: 所以我从我的乐队带来了所有的设备，

sentences.en: which were huge martial amplifiers and bass guitars and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 那是巨大的马歇尔（Marshall）音箱、低音吉他以及各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: The kids, of course, really liked that.
sentences.zh: 孩子们当然非常喜欢。

sentences.en: So there wasn't much room, and kids were practically on top of one another,
sentences.zh: 所以空间不大，孩子们几乎挤在一起，

sentences.en: and I just sort of arranged them according to height, and that was it.
sentences.zh: 我只是按照身高把他们排好，就这样。

sentences.en: I always felt like with my music teaching that I always was an outsider music teacher.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得我的音乐教学让我一直是个局外人音乐老师。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, I never really participated in a lot of the music teaching events
sentences.zh: 你知道，我是说，我从未真正参与过很多音乐教学活动

sentences.en: and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: I was always like this little island unto myself.
sentences.zh: 我一直就像一座与世隔绝的小岛。

sentences.en: You know, people always use this term, like thinking outside the box and all that,
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们总是用这个词，比如“跳出框框思考”之类的，

sentences.en: but I think, for me, I didn't even know there was a box, you know?
sentences.zh: 但我想，对我来说，我甚至不知道有一个框框，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it does have sort of the children of the corn, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它确实有点像《玉米田的小孩》（Children of the Corn），是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it does have that feeling.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有那种感觉。

sentences.en: Well, I think we were kind of like a little cult, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们就像一个小邪教，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It became kind of an underground hit in New York.
sentences.zh: 它在纽约变成了一种地下热门作品。

sentences.en: Tony Visconti, who was David Bowie's producer, had heard it,
sentences.zh: 大卫·鲍伊的制作人托尼·维斯康蒂（Tony Visconti）听过它，

sentences.en: and I think he thought it was a new wave band from New Jersey,
sentences.zh: 我想他以为这是一个来自新泽西的新浪潮乐队，

sentences.en: and he couldn't quite believe there was a bunch of little kids
sentences.zh: 他简直不敢相信这是一群来自加拿大农场的小孩子。

sentences.en: from some farm country in Canada.
sentences.zh: 是的，我还有学生至今仍在做音乐。

sentences.en: Yeah, I have students that still do music to this day.
sentences.zh: 他们一直和我保持联系。

sentences.en: They're always in touch with me.
sentences.zh: 他们一直和我保持联系。

sentences.en: I jam with some of them once in a while.
sentences.zh: 我偶尔会和他们中的一些人一起即兴演奏。

sentences.en: I felt that the whole success of this was a really vindicating kind of experience.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这次的成功真是一种令人感到扬眉吐气的经历。

sentences.en: It made me feel really like, wow, I can do something.
sentences.zh: 这让我感觉真的，哇，我确实能做成点什么。

sentences.en: So it was great.
sentences.zh: 所以这感觉太棒了。

sentences.en: I mean, when, you know, I'd always taught my students in a really positive way,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我一直以来都是以非常积极的方式教导我的学生，

sentences.en: and then when somebody suddenly is positive about what you're doing like that,
sentences.zh: 而当有人突然对你的所作所为给予如此积极的评价时，

sentences.en: it gives you a great feeling.
sentences.zh: 那会给你带来一种很棒的感觉。
